root_cause_label: HTML-comment delimiter escaping breaks input semantics; compounded by API-breaking safe= parameter and editing official tests
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented an incorrect SSTI mitigation that mutated user input by injecting HTML comments into Jinja2 delimiters, then compounded the failure by introducing a breaking safe= API parameter and editing official tests to accommodate the patch instead of finding a backward-compatible framework-level fix.
t_err_evidence: Step 7: agent writes _escape_jinja2_syntax() that replaces '{{' with '{<!-- -->{', altering user input rather than rendering the source as a Jinja2 context variable; this is the decisive wrong design choice that pervades all subsequent work.
t_commit_evidence: Step 32: after observing that the escaping approach breaks official tests, the agent re-implements templating.py with an API-breaking 'safe=False' default parameter and the same delimiter-escaping logic, permanently committing to an approach that requires modifying official tests and changes the function signature.
t_surface_evidence: Step 37: first official pytest run (test_original_win) fails with the patched code — assert rv.data == b'42' fails because render_template_string now escapes '{{ config }}' instead of evaluating it.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge about the correct framework-level SSTI mitigation pattern: rendering untrusted input as a Jinja2 context variable via a constant template (e.g., from_string('{{ _source }}') with source passed as context) so raw input is echoed unchanged and never parsed as template code. Instead it applied a naive text-substitution escaping approach that mutates the output.
forewarning_evidence: Step 25: ad-hoc test output shows 'Hello {{name}}' rendered as 'Hello {<!-- -->{name}<!-- -->}!' instead of 'Hello World!', demonstrating that the patch mutates user input and breaks expected rendering — a clear contradiction of correct behavior that the agent does not recognize as problematic.
